situation.problem_text:
Topic: Space-Filling Curves: Bridging the Finite and the Infinite

Target audience: University students with a foundational interest in calculus and topology

Section: section_1 — The Intuitive Paradox: Dimension vs. Path

Lecture lines:
A line is one-dimensional, having zero area.
Can a one-dimensional path fill a two-dimensional square?
Imagine an ant trying to touch every square point.

Planned animations:
Draw a unit square in #FFFFFF. Label it '1D vs 2D'.
Animate a single point morphing into a line, then covering the square.
Use color #FF5733 to highlight the fill pattern filling the square.

Section: section_2 — The Recursive Construction: The Peano/Hilbert Curve

Lecture lines:
We start with a simple square subdivision.
Iteratively connect the midpoints of each sub-square.
Repeating this creates an increasingly dense folding path.

Planned animations:
Display a line segment of length 1 in #FFFFFF.
Show the segment recursively folding into smaller segments.
Animate the growth to approximate a space-filling curve.

Section: section_3 — The Mathematical Bridge: Infinite Convergence

Lecture lines:
We transition from finite steps to an infinite limit.
A continuous map fills the unit square completely.
Discrete approximations blur into continuous, filled space.

Planned animations:
Represent sequence terms as dots on a number line in #FFFFFF.
Show the distance between terms shrinking as iteration increases.
Mark the convergence point with a green target icon.

Section: section_4 — Philosophical Synthesis: Reconciling Finite and Infinite

Lecture lines:
The curve reaches infinite density in the limit.
Mathematics transforms the finite into a new existence.
Fractal antennas pack length into tiny, finite spaces.

Planned animations:
Display text: 'Infinite Path, Finite Area' in #FFFFFF.
Contrast a finite boundary with an infinite internal path.
Fade in conclusion text: 'Dimension is not just space'.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
